previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, a mechanical aortic valve on anticoagulation, and multiple cardiovascular and vascular comorbidities was admitted for melena and weakness following a recent hospitalization for gastrointestinal bleeding. Her INR was elevated at 4.3, and she received two units of packed red blood cells initially, with a total of five units during the admission. Evaluation with EGD, capsule endoscopy, and a tagged red blood cell scan showed no active bleeding source, though mild duodenitis was noted. Warfarin was held and a heparin drip initiated, then transitioned to warfarin 3 mg daily as the INR stabilized. Her hemoglobin remained stable above 8 g/dL for over 72 hours prior to discharge. Hypocalcemia was managed with new prescriptions for calcitriol and calcium carbonate. She had a minor fall during admission, resulting in bedside wound debridement by vascular surgery. She was discharged home with home health services, instructions to monitor for recurrent bleeding, check INR on schedule, and follow up with GI, vascular surgery, and primary care.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ with ESRD s/p 2 failed renal transplants on home HD, CAD s/p 
CABG/AVR, afib, diastolic heart failure, prior CVAs, 
calciphylaxis, recent admission for GI bleed who presented with 
unstable angina and was found to have NSTEMI.
 
#) NSTEMI: Patient presented with NSTEMI, as evidenced by chest 
pain and elevated troponins without EKG changes in the setting 
of labile blood pressures. Initially, catheterization was 
deferred given elevated INR and hemodynamic instability. The 
patient was placed on a nitroglycerin gtt. This was titrated to 
chest pain free and initially was effective, however, shortly 
after initiation, the patient continued to have chest pain. Over 
the first 2 days of the ___ stay in the ICU, the nitro gtt 
was intermittently turned off but was continually reinitiated 
due to pain. The patient was also started on isordil and 
hydrazine for afterload reduction. These helped as well but 
still were not reliable in relieving her chest pain. The patient 
was taken for cath on ___ and found to have a new LAD lesion.  
A DES was successfully placed in the LAD and subsequently, the 
patient was chest pain free.  Isordil and hydrazine were 
discontinued.  She was started on plavix and aspirin and bridged 
to warfarin with heparin. The aspirin is planned to be 
discontinued after 1 month of therapeutic INR on warfarin, per 
Dr. ___ outpatient cardiologist. Given her risk for 
GI bleed, new INR goal will be 1.8-2.5 per discussion with Dr. 
___ Dr. ___ outpatient nephrologist.  

# HTN: Patient is known to have labile blood pressures. The 
___ systolic pressures ranged widely and occasionally 
hypertensive episodes were accompanied by chest pain (prior to 
placement of the stent). She also has significant sensitivity to 
antihypertensives and SBP would sometimes drop to ___ with 
small doses of nitrates or labetalol. Her home labetalol was 
continued and amlodipine was started with stability of her SBP 
in the 130-150 range. Antihypertensives were held for SBP<130, 
as she usually feels lightheaded when her SBP is below 120.

#) ACUTE DECOMPENSATED DIASTOLIC HEART FAILURE: LVEF >=55% on 
TTE during this admission. Patient presented with vascular 
congestion on chest xray and dyspnea on admission, likely from 
volume overload after her previous admission for GI bleed. She 
was dialyzed while admitted x 3 initially with removal of ultra 
filtrate and then with true HD. The patient initially had an O2 
requirement on admission but was sating well on room air by day 
of discharge. Discharge weight was 59kg.
  
# Question of pneumonia: Patient had CXR with findings 
suggestive of right middle/lower lung PNA and was given 
vancomycin/cefepime. She was subsequently afebrile and without 
cough or focal findings on lung exam, thus antibiotics were 
discontinued on hospital day 3.

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Ms. ___, 

You were admitted to the hospital because of chest pain you were 
having during dialysis. We found that your troponins were 
elevated. This indicates there might have been damage to your 
heart which is why you were observed in the cardiac ICU. We put 
you on medications to control your chest pain, and you underwent 
a coronary angiography.  A stent was placed in one of your 
coronary arteries to open a blockage.  Your chest pain resolved 
after this.  

You will need to take aspirin, plavix, and warfarin after you 
are discharged.  Your new INR goal is above 1.8, ideally in the 
1.8 to 2.5 range.  1 month after your INR is therapeutic, you 
can discontinue your aspirin.

You also received dialysis while you were admitted and had 
several liters of excess fluid removed.  

Please follow up with the providers listed below and continue 
taking your medications as prescribed. 

It was a pleasure taking care of you,
Your ___ Care Team
